question: How much of each salt was dissolved per litre to make the three forward osmosis draw solutions, and to what osmotic pressure?
expect: NaCl 35.0 g/L, MgSO4.7H2O 71.8 g/L, sodium acetate 79.4 g/L, each to 30 bar at 25 C (sec. 2.2)
rendered:
To find the concentration of each draw solution, we need to look at the section of the document where the draw solutions are described:

"Draw solutions were prepared to provide an initial nominal osmotic pressure of 30 bar at 25 °C, using analytical-grade salts: NaCl (35.0 g L^−1), MgSO4·7H2O (71.8 g L^−1), and sodium acetate (79.4 g L^−1)."

So, to make the three forward osmosis draw solutions, the following amounts of each salt were dissolved per liter:

- NaCl: 35.0 g/L
- MgSO4·7H2O: 71.8 g/L
- Sodium acetate: 79.4 g/L

The osmotic pressure was 30 bar.
